HISTORICAL PREDICTION · NOT INCREMENTAL SALES

One more item.
A different objective.

Rank possible food additions by historical purchase rate × unit gross margin, then compare against popularity. Customer confirmation and a controlled test come before a real offer.

June masked-basket evaluation

How to test incremental profit

Randomize eligible baskets to no prompt, a popular-item prompt or the margin-weighted rule. Log exposures, availability, actual completed purchases and basket gross profit. Account for prompt cost and purchases that would happen anyway. Historical retrieval does not estimate this treatment effect.

ACCOUNTING SENSITIVITY · DEMAND RESPONSE UNKNOWN

Can a tiny change
find one dollar?

Find the smallest whole-cent price increase within a defined branch-wide policy that would add at least $1/day if quantities, mix, unit costs and discount percentages stay fixed.

Other small single-product candidates

CANDIDATE SEARCH · NOT A SUBSTITUTION MODEL

A product is unavailable.
What might replace it?

Find same-category products with similar historical hourly selling patterns. Similarity does not mean customers will switch, and no unavailable-product sales are automatically reassigned.

Ingredient memberships are illustrative serving-equivalent assumptions, not verified recipes or allergen information. Actual recipe and inventory data are required before a real substitution.

ASSUMED SCENARIO · NO VALIDATED WAR PREDICTION

Constrained resources.
A plan you can inspect.

Compare popularity-based stocking, margin-based stocking and a constrained menu/stock optimizer under identical scenario assumptions. Every policy pays for all units stocked, including unsold units.

Optimized stock at the selected branch

Budget, capacity and assumed ingredient limits
Scenarios use a July 1 historical forecast from records through June 30. They are precomputed examples, not live operations. A closure assumes zero customer migration; a takeaway switch holds total expected units constant. No automatic substitution, real recipes, actual inventory, staff costs or measured stock transfers are present. Terminal salvage is assumed zero. A real crisis may invalidate every demand assumption.


Keep the root-cause investigation first.
These are testable extensions. None proves additional dollars from a promotion, diagnoses a supplier problem or validates performance during war. Separate measured historical results from assumed financial outcomes.
